propositions: Inventories are measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
NRV is estimated selling price less estimated completion and sale costs.
Inventory cost includes purchase costs, conversion costs and other costs to bring inventories to their present location and condition.
The carrying amount of inventory sold is recognised as expense when the related revenue is recognised.

official_external_sources.proposition: NRV is reassessed each subsequent period. A write-down is reversed only when the original circumstances no longer exist or clear evidence shows an NRV increase from changed economic circumstances; the reversal is limited to the original write-down so the new carrying amount remains the lower of cost and revised NRV.
official_external_sources.scope_limit: The task verified this public paragraph and the worked numbers only; it did not claim a paragraph-by-paragraph audit of the entire 2026 standard.

propositions: Policies developed with judgement must result in relevant and reliable information.
Changes in estimates arise from new information or new developments and are not corrections of errors.
Prior-period errors include omissions and misstatements arising from failure to use or misuse of available reliable information.
official_external_sources.supporting_location: IAS 8 paragraphs 32-34 state that estimates use latest reliable information and that reasonable estimates are an essential part of preparing financial statements.

official_external_sources.location: IFRS 9 paragraphs 5.5.1 and 5.5.17; trade-receivable application within the expected-credit-loss requirements
official_external_sources.proposition: An entity recognises a loss allowance for expected credit losses on applicable financial assets. Expected credit losses are measured using unbiased probability weighting, time value of money, and reasonable and supportable past, current and forward-looking information.
official_external_sources.scope_limit: Used only to support the ECL distinction and the loss-allowance teaching card; no full IFRS 9 measurement model is claimed.

official_external_sources.proposition: The depreciation method reflects the pattern in which the asset's future economic benefits are expected to be consumed and is reviewed at least at each financial year-end; a changed pattern is treated as a change in accounting estimate under IAS 8.

Cash comprises cash on hand and demand deposits; cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid investments readily convertible to known amounts of cash and subject to insignificant value-change risk.
official_external_sources.supporting_proposition: Cash equivalents are held for short-term cash commitments, and the normal three-month guide runs from acquisition to maturity.

official_external_sources.location: Demand Deposits with Restrictions on Use (IAS 7), agenda decision
official_external_sources.proposition: A third-party contractual restriction does not by itself remove a demand deposit from cash unless it changes the nature of the deposit; separate presentation, current/non-current classification and restricted-cash disclosures remain separate questions.

A liability is current when it is expected to settle in the normal operating cycle, held primarily for trading, due within twelve months, or the entity lacks a reporting-date right to defer settlement for at least twelve months. Operating-cycle items can be current even if settled after twelve months.
IFRS 18 replaces IAS 1 for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, with earlier application permitted.
official_external_sources.scope_limit: The note's 2026 teaching supplement uses IAS 1 unless early application facts say otherwise.

official_external_sources.proposition: Trade payables concern received goods or services that are invoiced or formally agreed; accruals concern received goods or services not yet paid, invoiced or formally agreed, and may require estimates whose uncertainty is generally less than provisions.
A contract liability is the entity's obligation to transfer goods or services for consideration already received or due.

official_external_sources.issuer: US Securities and Exchange Commission, Office of Investor Education and Advocacy
official_external_sources.proposition: Private placements can include notes or bonds, so a bond is not necessarily issued to the public or freely transferable.
